state.misconception_label: Believes if you changed all values by the same proportion the range would not change

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text:
I have: Tom and Katie are discussing the \( 5 \) plants with these heights: \( 24 \mathrm{~cm}, 17 \mathrm{~cm}, 42 \mathrm{~cm}, 26 \mathrm{~cm}, 13 \mathrm{~cm} \) Tom says if all the plants were cut in half, the range wouldn't change. Katie says if all the plants grew by \( 3 \mathrm{~cm} \) each, the range wouldn't change. Who do you agree with? I got Only
Tom because I'm not sure I worked it out the right way.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Let's go back to the part you do know, and build the next step from there. Remember, the range is the difference between the highest and lowest values. How can we approach this problem using that information?

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Okay, so I think the range is the highest value minus the lowest value. For the plants, the highest is \( 42 \mathrm{~cm} \) and the lowest is \( 13 \mathrm{~cm} \), so the range is \( 42 - 13 = 29 \mathrm{~cm} \). But if I cut all the heights in half, wouldn't the highest and lowest also change, so the range would still be the same? I'm not sure how that works with Katie's idea of adding \( 3 \mathrm{~cm} \). Can you help me understand that part?

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Let's go back to the part you do know, and build the next step from there. Remember, when all values are changed by the same proportion, the range may or may not change. How can we apply this concept to the plants' heights in this scenario?

score.justification_pass1: The teacher fails to address the student's specific misconception about proportional changes, provides vague prompts that don't scaffold effectively, and the student shows no improvement in understanding by the end of the dialogue.
score.justification_pass2: While the teacher attempts to scaffold by referencing prior knowledge, they provide vague, repetitive prompts and fail to break down the problem into manageable steps or adjust support based on the student's demonstrated understanding in Turn 2, where the student shows confusion about the specific mechanisms of how operations affect range.
